answer: Each lantern is one forged identity. Quartz is the register where rows are etched, on a plate whose burn cannot be cloned in software. A row opens only when its host burns in a relic: a one-time token the attestation destroys, so no relic ever backs two rows, and a rented host has none to burn. Every relic drawn from the one global stock of unspent devices thins that stock, so the thousandth lantern pays far more trade credit than the first, and parallel bidding lifts every clone's price alike. It breaks if a relic can be copied in software or issued on demand.
